subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up: latency/throughput/concurrency
messages:

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: benchmark methodology & SLOs (recap + next steps)

Hi Alex / Sreya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about EdgeFin's realtime scoring use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point for the benchmark: 

- Scope: online scoring for short-form financial summaries (avg ~80 tokens output), token-level streaming required for UX.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms end-to-end for streaming (token-first-byte to full-response completion is acceptable for overall SLA; we should also capture token-emission latency for streaming UX).
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline concurrency 50 sustained, burst up to 200 concurrent request contexts. Typical QPS now ~60, expect to scale to ~300 within 6 months.
- Quality: use your canonical prompt/templates and our shared eval harness. We'll compare model variants at matched cost points.

Action items I propose:
1) You share the canonical prompt set and a sample trace (we can use your real traces or synthetic variants) — we'll use these to reproduce workload characteristics.
2) We exchange measurement definitions (what we measure for p95/p99, sampling windows, warm vs cold starts).
3) Schedule a joint benchmark run in your staging (we can run from our Dedicated infra or in your VPC depending on preference).

I've attached an initial prompt set (v1) and added a Drive folder with the benchmark template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cBenchmarkDocs

If that looks right, can you confirm the latency targets above and share the sample trace and any constraints (is GPU isolation required? do you have TLS-only egress, IP allowlists, etc.)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if useful.

Best,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: benchmark methodology & SLOs (recap + next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming streaming is required: we need token-by-token delivery to the frontend, p95 token-emission latency should be <= 120ms for the first substantive token, and full-response p99 <= 350ms is acceptable.
- Concurrency: 50 sustained is accurate; ability to handle spikes to 200 with graceful degradation is important (we prefer tail-latency controls over dropped requests).
- QPS: current steady-state ~60 QPS, but many of those are bursty at market open; we'd like to see behavior under heavy fan-in.

Regarding the benchmark inputs: sharing a sanitized sample trace now (attached) and our canonical prompt set — note that prompts include dynamic slot-filling and some multi-turn context (~3 prior turns). We care about reproducibility (same seed, deterministic sampling where applicable) and repeatability across runs.

We also need to understand how you report costs (tokens vs request-seconds) and whether the benchmark will include prewarming/priming overheads.

Attaching: edgefin_sample_trace.json, prompt_set_edgefin_v1.csv

Alex
CTO, EdgeFin
alex.park@edgefin.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-16T09:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: benchmark methodology & SLOs (recap + next steps)

Appreciate the details, Alex — this is exactly the kind of stuff we need. I've pulled together a short methodology doc and a formal measurement definitions PDF (attached) that we use internally for performance SLO benchmarking. Key highlights: 

- Measurement definitions:
  - "Token-emission latency" = time from request accepted to first token bytes emitted.
  - "Response completion latency" = time from request accepted to final token emitted.
  - Percentiles are calculated on completed requests over a 5-minute sampling window (we'll share raw traces for verification).
- Streaming: we capture token emission times and tail behavior; we also report per-token inter-arrival percentiles to surface jitter.
- Warm vs cold: we run 3 warmup passes (discarded) followed by 5 measured runs. For cold-start characterization we force no-cache runs (cold VM + kernel cold-start).
- Reproducibility: we fix RNG seeds, pin model weights/quantization profile, and provide the prompt set (see updated benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv attached). We also include a small harness (link in Drive) so you can run the same commands locally.

Next steps:
- We'll run an internal lab run this Friday against a Dedicated instance (same model classes we discussed) using your attached trace and prompt set v2.
- Propose a joint run next Tuesday 2026-07-21 16:00 PT — we can stream metrics to the Drive folder and do a live post-mortem.

I've attached: redwood_benchmark_guidelines.pdf and benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv. Let me know if you need us to run inside your VPC (we can arrange an ephemeral worker) or if you prefer we run from Redwood Dedicated infra.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_guidelines.pdf, benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv
